In the bustling heart of Tokyo, where neon lights painted the night sky in a kaleidoscope of colors, Eon Takahashi lived a life as ordinary as they come. At 28 years old, he was a mid-level software engineer at a tech firm, spending his days debugging code and his evenings binge-watching isekai anime. He loved those stories—the ones where everyday protagonists got yanked into fantastical worlds, armed with cheat skills and destined for greatness. "If only," he'd mutter to himself, slurping instant ramen in his cramped apartment, surrounded by posters of sword-wielding heroes and busty elf maidens. Little did he know, the universe—or whatever chaotic force governed it—had a twisted sense of humor.

It happened on a rainy Tuesday evening. Eon was walking home from the office, umbrella in one hand and his phone in the other, scrolling through Reddit threads about the latest truck-kun memes. The streets were slick with puddles reflecting the city lights, and the air hummed with the distant roar of traffic. He stepped off the curb at a crosswalk, his mind wandering to the plot of his favorite show, where the hero summoned infinite mana from a void god. "Man, what if that happened to me?" he chuckled aloud.

Then, without warning, the world tilted. A blinding flash erupted around him—not from a truck, but from nowhere at all. It felt like the fabric of reality was unraveling, threads pulling him apart and stitching him back together in an instant. His stomach lurched, his vision blurred into a vortex of swirling colors, and a deafening roar filled his ears, like the scream of a thousand eldritch horrors. Eon's last coherent thought was, "This can't be real..."

When the chaos subsided, Eon found himself sprawled on damp earth, not concrete. The rain had stopped, replaced by a gentle mist that clung to his skin. He blinked, pushing himself up on shaky arms, and took in his surroundings. Towering trees loomed overhead, their leaves a vibrant green that shimmered with an otherworldly glow. The air smelled of pine and something metallic—magic? No skyscrapers, no honking cars, no glowing billboards. Instead, a dirt path wound through the forest, flanked by ferns and glowing mushrooms that pulsed with faint blue light. In the distance, he heard the hoot of an unfamiliar bird and the rustle of leaves that sounded too deliberate, like something—or someone—was watching.
